change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator can't page a datetime key, so the optimized audit-log path returns 500
findings.body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies the integer `Paginator.get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor`. The audit-log endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"` (organization_auditlogs.py:80).

- **Item key:** `getattr(item, "datetime")` is a `datetime`, so `math.ceil(value)` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key on the results (line 904), so any `?optimized_pagination=true` request that returns at least one row fails with a 500.
- **Cursor value:** `value_from_cursor` returns the raw millisecond integer. `build_queryset` then emits `datetime <= <int>`, comparing a timestamp column with an integer.

`DateTimePaginator` (paginator.py:230-241) converts in both directions. Subclass `DateTimePaginator` or reuse its key and value methods, and add a test that exercises this path.

findings.title: The negative-offset "advanced feature" can't work: Django querysets reject negative slices
findings.body:
Cursor offsets come straight from the client (`Cursor.from_string`, cursors.py:59), so `cursor=0:-5:0` reaches line 882 as `queryset[-5:...]`. Django `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for that.

This is not a `BadPaginationError`, so `paginate` (base.py:540) does not turn it into a 400; the request fails with a 500. The comment's claims are false: the ORM does not "handle negative slicing automatically", and nothing gives "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds".

Remove this branch, or reject negative offsets with a `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: BasePaginator only clamps negative offsets on next-page cursors; prev cursors still crash
findings.body:
This change to the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` affects every subclass (`Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and others).

- **Next cursors:** a negative offset is clamped to 0.
- **Prev cursors:** a negative offset is passed through unchanged. A client-supplied cursor such as `1:-1:1` still raises Django's negative-indexing `ValueError` and returns a 500.
- **Unchanged check:** line 192 still compares against `offset`, not `start_offset`.

The comment says negative offsets are allowed and "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions"; neither is true. Clamp in both directions, or raise `BadPaginationError` for `offset < 0`, so a malformed cursor gets a 400.

findings.title: The gate is not an admin check: has_global_access is open-membership access, and is_superuser skips active-superuser checks
findings.body:
The comment says the path is for "authorized administrators". It isn't restricted that way:

- **`member.has_global_access`:** any member of an org with open membership has it. It is not an admin role.
- **`request.user.is_superuser`:** Sentry elsewhere uses `is_active_superuser(request)`, which also requires an active superuser session. The bare flag skips that.

The queryset is already scoped to the organization, so no data crosses orgs today. If the path really needs a privilege gate, use the existing helpers. If it doesn't, drop the gate and the comment.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and the docstring claims features it doesn't have
findings.body:
Apart from the broken negative-offset branch, `get_result` (lines 845-911) is a copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`. There is no "optimized query path" and no "streamlined boundary handling".

The comment added in cursors.py:26-27 is also wrong: the `Cursor` constructor has always accepted any integer offset, so the change there is comment-only. Once the datetime and negative-slice bugs are fixed, the class adds nothing over `DateTimePaginator`; consider removing it and the query flag.

contracts.action: GET audit logs with ?optimized_pagination=true as superuser/global-access member
contracts.before_after: The equivalent path converts datetime to an ms int key and back (paginator.py:233-241). The new paginator does neither (paginator.py:838-843).
contracts.visible_effect: The response rows and Link cursor headers come from base.paginate (base.py:535-558).
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError in get_item_key on any non-empty page, and Django ValueError on a negative offset. Neither is caught by paginate (base.py:540), so the request fails with a 500.

summary: The new optimized audit-log pagination path can't work, and it adds a 500 where a 400 belongs. With `?optimized_pagination=true`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` applies integer key math to the `datetime` field, so any request that returns a row fails. Its negative-offset branch slices the Django queryset with a negative index, which Django rejects. The shared `BasePaginator` change clamps negative offsets on next-page cursors but still passes them through on previous-page cursors. The permission gate isn't an admin check, and the new comments and docstrings describe behaviour the code doesn't have.
